origin.rerun: grep -n 'def _open_trades' -A5 src/units/accounts/ib_client.py (holds while it returns [] on exception) and grep -n 'self._cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol(ib, sym)' src/units/accounts/ib_client.py (holds while _locked_close discards the result); reproduce with a FakeIB whose openTrades() raises -> _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol returns verify_state not_attempted, seen 0, no warning.

what: HIGH (code audit CA-A04): IBClient.close() can flatten while the protective bracket still rests. Step 1 (_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol, called at ib_client.py:2642 with its result DISCARDED) iterates self._open_trades(ib), which returns [] when ib.openTrades() raises (ib_client.py:4731-4735). A Gateway read failure therefore reads as 'nothing to cancel' — MEASURED with a raising fake: {'verify_state': 'not_attempted', 'seen': 0, 'cancelled': 0, 'failed': 0, 'account_wide_seen': None}, no exception, no warning — and Step 2 sends the opposing MarketOrder. The bracket left over a flat book can later fill and OPEN a reverse position: the BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP class, and the same outcome as CA-A01's critical oca-protect-t5836. The file already names this defect at ib_client.py:3355-3359 and works around it only in _sweep_stray_oca_groups. Same collapse feeds cancel_resting_protection (:3627) and _cancel_oca_group_for_symbol. FIX (Tier-2 order path): read ib.openTrades() directly in these two cancel helpers, return an 'unreadable' state, and have _locked_close defer (retCode 2) instead of flattening when Step 1 could not look. Found by a lane reader sub-agent; re-verified by the lane.
